<think>
The user asks: "Show the 10 processes using the most memory. Reply with only the command."

We need to produce a shell command that would show the top 10 processes by memory usage. The system is a Linux environment, presumably with standard commands like `ps`, `top`, `vmstat`, etc.

The typical way: `ps -eo comm,pcpu,mems,pid,schedid | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10`. That shows process name, CPU%, memory% (in KB), PID, etc. Or using `top` with `-b -n 10 -p $(cat /proc/self/status)` but that's more complex.

Simplest: `ps -eo comm,pcpu,mems,pid,schedid | sort -t, -k3 -nr | head -n 10`. That shows memory usage (mems column). Or we could use `top -bn1 | grep ' %MEM:'` but that's less precise.

Thus answer: just the command. No extra explanation. So:

`ps -eo comm,pcpu,mems,pid,schedid | sort -t, -k3 -nr | head -n 10`

That is a single line. That should satisfy. Ensure no extra text.
</think>
ps -eo comm,pcpu,mems,pid,schedid | sort -t, -k3 -nr | head -n 10
